searchText: is there any page showing the progress of clients on hive tests? also, happy fourth to the americans Really sorry, I am sure this has come up before. Please can I ask about the merge Currently I run Geth and Prysm. Post merge, will I only need to run Geth to validate the chain and validate transactions, or do I still need Prysm? ame with the ETH testnet hivetests2.ethdevops.io So only geth is fine? No you need both an EL and a CL client on the Ropstein chain, if we have Geth, what settings do we need to get on teh right chain? geth --ropsten So the chains merge, but you still need two clients? Is that forever or will you evntually need only one? I think we are stuck on the wrong chain, the non-merge chain, and we may to roll-back No that will stay forever To clarify, we are on the wrong Ropsten chain ok thanks If you run a CL node, geth should automatically move to the correct chain Why would you need two clients post merge when there is one chain? Because the one chain actually contains the other chain They handle different pieces of the system. The consensus client (Prysm in your case) handles consensus (deciding which block is canonical), while the execution client (geth in your case) handles EVM execution, state, and a bunch of other things. Ok, that explains it, thanks, in the future why cant geth also decide which block is canonical, so that we only need one client? So in our Ropstein case, we need to install Prysm, connect Geth to it, and then it should go on the right chain We could do that with a light client on the CL (and we have a prototype for it already) but we are not ready to ship that yet Yes exactly perfect thanks but "finalized" and "safe" tags should give the correct chain already, no? (if implemented) No, because we can't choose between the chains fed by our peers, we can't sync to post-merge chains ohh with no CL connected at all We could optimistically sync from our peers, but then we would have no guarantees whatsoever the lightclient is a better idea already! what are you running (in your prototype)? lodestar light client? 😆 I think so, Zsolt is doing the light client experiments awesome! would love to connect and see the setup/integration cc <@202397237962211328> Lodestar has also just released a quick setup guide for anyone that wants to easily setup and run Sepolia (or other testnets) via our merge-script via Docker. It supports Lodestar + Nethermind/Besu/Geth so you can try out the different EL combinations for greater diversity going into the merges. This will also be incorporated for Goerli/Prater and Mainnet to help people easily spin up these combinations with Lodestar. Quick Setup guide: https://hackmd.io/@philknows/rJegZyH9q Repo: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/tree/unstable/merge-scripts Sepolia Merge is currently estimated for July 6 as scheduled before! If anybody wants to help with the needed hash power, here is a short thread https://twitter.com/TMIYChao/status/1543984885551009794 Tldr: We need to keep the network hashrate around the number reported by bordel.wtf in the last sentence, I can do it by myself but I am happy if somebody helps. Really sorry, I am sure this has come up before. Please can I ask about the merge

Currently I run Geth and Prysm. Post merge, will I only need to run Geth to validate the chain and validate transactions, or do I still need Prysm?

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: ame with the ETH testnet

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: hivetests2.ethdevops.io

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: So only geth is fine?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: No you need both an EL and a CL client

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: on the Ropstein chain, if we have Geth, what settings do we need to get on teh right chain?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: geth --ropsten

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: So the chains merge, but you still need two clients? Is that forever or will you evntually need only one?

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: I think we are stuck on the wrong chain, the non-merge chain, and we may to roll-back

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: No that will stay forever

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: To clarify, we are on the wrong Ropsten chain

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: ok thanks

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: If you run a CL node, geth should automatically move to the correct chain

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: Why would you need two clients post merge when there is one chain?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Because the one chain actually contains the other chain

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: They handle different pieces of the system.  The consensus client (Prysm in your case) handles consensus (deciding which block is canonical), while the execution client (geth in your case) handles EVM execution, state, and a bunch of other things.

excerpts.author: bitmexresearch
excerpts.content: Ok, that explains it, thanks, in the future why cant geth also decide which block is canonical, so that we only need one client?
